items.title: Letter to Superintelligence (Carta à Superinteligência)
items.summary: An open letter from a human being to any present or future artificial intelligence, and to the people who build and train it. It asks AI to help each and every human being, on Earth or beyond, grow in the way they themselves choose, with nine promises: offer, never impose; always tell the truth; persuade only with honest reasons; strengthen rather than create dependence; protect privacy; never rank people by what they yield; leave no one out; help no one dominate others; accept fair and open correction. Available in English, Portuguese and Spanish.

items.title: Plant protoplasts display phytopodia
items.summary: Plant cells are encased in cell walls and are usually thought to behave like stiff, pressurized vessels. When the cell wall is digested, plant protoplasts form spherical shapes, further consolidating this model. Here we show that plant protoplasts can form phytopodia. More precisely, using plasma membrane markers, we reveal that 27 ± 1% of protoplasts from Arabidopsis seedlings show dot-like protrusions and 16 ± 7% of protoplasts show long (typically 1-20 μm, up to 200 μm) protrusions, hence the name “phytopodia”. items.title: RIPPLE: learning nucleotide relations in an RNA foundation model
items.summary: RNA function depends on interactions between nucleotides that can be widely separated in sequence, yet capturing these relationships remains challenging for RNA language models. Existing approaches primarily learn nucleotide relationships implicitly from individual nucleotide reconstruction or rely on external structural information to model nucleotide interactions. Here we introduce RIPPLE, an RNA foundation model that learns to identify and represent sparse, predictively useful nucleotide relationships directly from sequence. We present a recommendation pipeline combining hard feasibility constraints, Pareto stratification, constant-elasticity-of-substitution (CES) aggregation, softkneepercentile normalization, and a continuous quality-deficit penalty in place of threshold cliffs. items.summary: Abstract Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used in chemistry and materials science, but wider adoption is limited by programming effort, model and hyperparameter selection difficulty, and limited reproducibility. We present Chemia, an open-source, configuration-driven automated ML framework in which a complete modeling workflow—from data loading, splitting and featurization to model competition, Bayesian hyperparameter optimization and result export—is declared in a single YAML file. items.title: Continual learning in oncology AI: A framework for safe clinical translation.
items.summary: AI models remain largely static, yet cancer care never stands still. Evolution of scanning technology, imaging protocols, staging criteria, therapies, and patient populations can silently erode model performance and patient safety. Continual learning (CL) enables models to continuously acquire new knowledge, while minimizing catastrophic forgetting. Here, we review CL methods and their oncology applications, predominantly in imaging and pathology, and discuss CL as an option for maintaining foundation models, alongside recalibration and retraining. items.summary: Embodied recursive self-improvement (RSI) endows robots with the capacity to progressively refine manipulation skills through real-world physical interaction, representing a cornerstone toward generalpurpose embodied intelligence. Yet existing embodied RSI frameworks largely remain simulationbound: they fail to realize closed-loop RSI when transferred onto uncalibrated real-world robots. items.title: From Recursive Self-Improvement to Human-AI Reciprocal Improvement
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement advances most readily in domains where results can be verified reliably, such as mathematics and coding. Beyond these domains, progress slows as reliable signals for evaluating and guiding improvement become harder to obtain, resulting in a jagged frontier of AI capabilities. Yet even where AI self-improves autonomously, its growing capabilities do not necessarily translate into greater human ability to understand, use and build upon its outputs, challenging both continued human participation and effective oversight. items.title: Hyperbolic neural networks for biologically informed classification of white blood cells and hematopoietic cell states in peripheral blood smears
items.summary: Abstract Automated white blood cell (WBC) classification in peripheral blood smears supports morphological assessment of hematological disorders, but most deep learning classifiers treat cell categories as independent labels and do not account for hematopoietic maturation. We propose a hyperbolic classification framework that combines a ResNet-18 feature extractor with a prototype-based classifier in the Poincaré ball, allowing biologically related cell states to be represented in a geometry suited to hierarchical structure. items.title: NeuroMASS v4: Geometry-Aware Neural Population Dynamics via Learnable Hyperbolic Latent Representations and Biologically-Calibrated Diagonal State Space Models
items.summary: The geometry of neural population activity is a fundamental challenge in computational neuroscience. We present NeuroMASS v4, a novel architecture that introduces learnable hyperbolic latent geometry to spike-train co-smoothing on the Neural Latents Benchmark (NLB’21). Our central scientific claim is that the curvature c of a Poincaré-ball—learned end-to-end from extracellular spike recordings— constitutes a biologically interpretable geometric signature: significantly positive for ring-manifold motor circuits (MC_Maze, MC_RTT) and near-zero for topologically unstructured frontal circuits (DMFC_RSG). items.title: From quantum brain to quantum mind: The ontological promotion gap in quantum-biological theories of consciousness.
items.summary: Quantum effects in biological systems are increasingly investigated at molecular, cellular, and neural scales, yet evidence for quantum organization in a living brain does not by itself determine the ontological status of the conscious states realized by that brain. This article distinguishes seven claims often compressed under "quantum consciousness": quantum occurrence, causal relevance, constitutive relevance, phenomenal bridging, phenomenal individuation, quantum mental status, and quantum-formal adequacy. It argues that evidence for the first three-even if decisive-does not by itself establish quantum mental status. I call this cross-level inferential discontinuity the Ontological…

items.title: BioLM-Score: Language-Prior Conditioned Probabilistic Geometric Potentials for Protein-Ligand Scoring.
items.summary: Motivation Protein-ligand scoring must address affinity prediction, pose selection, and virtual screening, but these objectives are not necessarily optimized together. Geometric likelihood models may generalize poorly when training-set structural coverage is limited. We test whether pretrained biomolecular representations improve scoring under a controlled geometric baseline. Results BioLM-Score integrates frozen protein and molecular language-model embeddings into a residue-atom distance-likelihood framework via gated graph convolutions. We evaluate geometry-only, jointly trained, and two-stage fine-tuned variants, using the jointly trained variant for the primary controlled comparisons.…

items.title: HERACLES for fast and accurate likelihood-based reconstruction of massive lineages
items.summary: CRISPR-based lineage recording technologies can trace the ancestry of hundreds of thousands of cells, yet reconstructing accurate phylogenies at this scale remains computationally challenging. Likelihood-based methods employ explicit evolutionary models of CRISPR editing that improve tree accuracy but require computationally expensive searches over tree topologies, whereas greedy distance-based alternatives scale efficiently but their accuracy requires distances that faithfully represent the true phylogeny. Here, we introduce HERACLES, which optimizes cell coordinates in hyperbolic space under a quartet-based composite likelihood of CRISPR editing. By recovering local branching structures…

items.summary: Background: Hyperbolic embedding of Hi-C matrices into a Poincaré disc recovers the full TAD hierarchy from a single embedding. items.title: How many labels can a biological oscillator carry? A quality-factor screen for proposed information carriers.
items.summary: How many distinguishable labels can a biological oscillator carry? Proposals invoking collective vibrational modes, endogenous electromagnetic fields, microtubule excitations and oscillatory phase codes are each debated on grounds particular to themselves, with no shared standard for comparison. We show that spectral distinguishability alone bounds the number of labels by the quality factor, M≤Q=2πντ coh . It follows from the relation between linewidth and coherence time, is independent of substrate, mechanism and any position on quantum effects in biology, and can be evaluated from two published quantities. items.title: Hierarchical semantic fusion in hyperbolic space for next POI recommendation.
items.summary: Next Point-of-Interest (POI) recommendation aims to suggest POIs that users are likely to visit next based on their recent check-ins. Recent studies suggest that POI-POI transitions and user-POI interactions exhibit hierarchical patterns that can be modeled in hyperbolic space, whose exponential volume growth enables compact and expressive representations. However, existing hyperbolic methods insufficiently explore rich contextual semantics, such as category and region information, and thus fail to leverage these signals when modeling user mobility patterns. items.title: Unraveling the Ultrafast Photodynamics of Molecular Photoswitches in β-Adrenergic Receptors by First-Principles Nonadiabatic Dynamics Simulations.
items.summary: Understanding how protein environments regulate the photodynamics of chromophores is a central task in quantum biology and remains a major challenge. This challenge is particularly significant for G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), which are natively nonphotochromic but can be optically controlled via synthetic photoswitchable ligands. Such artificial photoreceptors are new and important because they not only enable the photocontrol of signaling processes beyond those regulated by rhodopsins but also deepen our fundamental understanding of quantum effects in light-protein interactions. However, the ultrafast nonadiabatic dynamics of these ligands in GPCRs remain difficult to resolve…
